title: Adequate representation
summary: Adequate representation protects absentees by requiring representatives and counsel capable of pursuing the class’s interests without disqualifying conflicts. It is central to the legitimacy of binding people who do not appear individually.
notes: A representative’s assurance of fairness does not itself resolve a fundamental allocation conflict. Subclasses with appropriate independent representation may be necessary, depending on the setting.

sections.Meaning: Adequate representation protects absentees by requiring representatives and counsel capable of pursuing the class’s interests without disqualifying conflicts. It is central to the legitimacy of binding people who do not appear individually.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify whose interests the representatives advance, any materially different groups within the class, and counsel’s ability and incentives. Hansberry addresses opposing interests; Amchem and Ortiz require structural protection for conflicting claimant groups.
